core: Meter as recurring beat grouping and hierarchy
Distinctions among beat, meter, rhythm, tempo, and time signature
Simple-meter time-signature conventions in common Western notation
supporting: Accents and downbeats as evidence for, rather than synonyms of, meter
outOfScope: Detailed compound-meter, irregular-meter, and changing-meter instruction
Conducting technique and advanced rhythmic transcription
Claims that all music foregrounds a stable or easily counted meter

claims.claim: Meter concerns the way a musical pulse is grouped, while a beat is the underlying recurring pulse.
Introductory Western-music terminology identifies recurring groupings of two, three, and four beats as duple, triple, and quadruple meter.
A measure or bar is one written group of beats, and bar lines separate measures in common Western notation.
In simple meters, a time signature communicates beats per measure through its top number and the note value used as the beat unit through its bottom number.
A simple-meter time signature is a notation convention rather than an arithmetic fraction.
The sources treat the first beat of a grouping as relatively strong or as a downbeat, while syncopation can redirect emphasis away from expected metrical strength.
Rhythm describes durations and placements of events, whereas meter supplies a recurring beat-grouping framework; tempo concerns the rate of the beat.
